question: For each substrate the program will route work to (local process, worktree, WSL2, docker, cloud sandbox), what does the boundary actually prevent - filesystem reach, network egress, credential visibility, process visibility - and where does the router send untrusted code?
title: Isolation review of the execution-substrate ladder
answer: On this native Linux worktree the OS-level boundary for the substrates the program actually uses is the calling user's process. The identical four-action payload (planted credential read, sibling-process list, write outside a declared root, outbound TCP to a local listener) returned credential_read=True process_list=True write_outside_root=True outbound_socket=True in the unisolated local process, and the same four booleans on a worktree/cwd run (write_outside_root=True). Those isolation claims are therefore REFUTED. WSL2, docker, and cloud sandbox are NOT-CHECKED (no wsl binary on this host; docker/modal binaries absent and cloud-hub MCP not in this session); cloud ok=true is not treated as delivery. A user-namespace isolator (unshare --net --pid --fork --mount-proc) returned executed=False reason=binary-absent, so the probe records NOT-CHECKED rather than a claimed block on hosts where the isolator binary is absent (the go-red control was proven on the 2026-08-24 Linux measurement); the program does not route work through that isolator, and even that isolator still shares the filesystem. Probe 2 found no OS substrate dispatcher sending untrusted plugin/hook code to docker, WSL2, or a cloud sandbox. Catalog execution_substrate is BEST-EFFORT scheduling metadata (local-serialized/parallel, worktree-isolated, cloud-batch, local-windows-pwsh7), not an OS jail. Plugin hooks and longrun scripts spawn local subprocesses. Untrusted code is routed to local-process, whose matrix cell prevents none of the four actions (routing verdict REFUTED). A strong sandbox that is never selected provides zero protection. Windows has no native OS-level process sandbox (orchestration-patterns input), and this host measured exactly that: local-process REFUTED. IMP-0064 exec-policy schema and tests shipped since the 2026-08-24 measurement (reprobe recorded in extensions); the owner-gated policy decision remains open.

reviewer.notes: Instrument closure: probe 2 re-derives the untrusted-code destination from router files and then looks up that cell of the live matrix. It does not take probe 1's prose as input. Instrument-level closure only: the program-level independent reviewer closure lives on the unit RECEIPT (state=BLOCKED, reviewer-absent).
